title: Getting Started: Apps, Plans, and Usage Limits

questions.prompt: Where do you find tools like web search, connectors, and Research in the message box?

options.text: In the + menu in the lower left (or by typing /)
They're only available through the API

questions.explanation: The + button in the lower left of the message box, or typing /, opens additional options and commands, including tools and connectors.

questions.prompt: Which of these use more of your usage limit? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The Help Center lists message length, attachment size, conversation length, tool use such as Research and web search, model choice, effort level, Artifacts, and multi-step tasks as factors that consume more usage.

questions.prompt: Paid plans have a session limit that resets every ____ hours, plus weekly limits.
questions.explanation: Paid plans have a five-hour session limit and weekly limits; Free also has a session limit that resets every five hours.

questions.prompt: Match each plan to who it fits best.

pairs.right: Heavy individual use with 5x or 20x Pro's usage
Small and mid-size teams with shared projects and admin controls

questions.explanation: Free is for trying Claude, Pro for regular individuals, Max for heavy users (5x or 20x Pro's usage), and Team for organizations that need collaboration and admin controls.

questions.prompt: Order these steps for deciding whether to upgrade your plan.

items.text: Use your current plan for a couple of weeks
Check Settings > Usage to see how much you actually use
Note whether you regularly run out before the limits reset

questions.explanation: The lesson's advice is to check real usage in Settings > Usage over a couple of weeks before upgrading, and to upgrade only if you consistently run out.

questions.prompt: On a Pro or Max plan, how is Claude Code usage counted?

options.text: It shares the same usage limits as your Claude chats
It has a completely separate, unlimited allowance
It's always billed at API rates

questions.explanation: The Help Center says these limits are shared across Claude and Claude Code, so all activity in both counts against the same limits.
